title: OpenAI compatibility: function routing, ambiguity disambiguation, and framed tool-message protocol
author: Marta Liu
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: clarify tool selection semantics and introduce framed tool-message protocol for streaming tool outputs. Backwards-compatible routing; mitigations for ambiguous tool_choice values.
Improves reliability of tool invocation streaming and structured output mapping.
description: Motivation: openai-style function/tool calling integration has subtle mismatches with Redwood's router and streaming layer. This PR defines a compact, backwards-compatible framing for partial tool messages so streamed invocations can be reassembled reliably by clients, aligns the tool schema mapping to Redwood's structured-output descriptors, and tightens tool_choice semantics to be deterministic when model signals are ambiguous. Changes include: 1) a specification for a minimal framing envelope inserted into streamed tool outputs so fragments contain tool_id, sequence_idx and a finality flag; 2) a router rule update that prefers explicit tool_id signals, falls back to schema-compatibility score if tool_choice is null/ambiguous, and exposes debug_reason on routed responses; 3) a mapping layer that converts OpenAI-style JSON-schema tool definitions into Redwood structured-output descriptors (type, required, constraints, example) and validates request/response against the mapped schema at call time; 4) new end-to-end tests for streaming reassembly, schema-validation failure modes, and ambiguous-tool fallbacks; 5) SDK helpers in python/ts to parse framed streams and surface partial tool payloads with progress events. Checklist: - [x] Spec document for framed tool messages included - [x] Implementation in openai_compat router + streaming codec - [x] Schema mapper and validation with clear error codes - [x] Unit/integration tests (including flaky test flake guard) - [x] SDK helpers and docs snippets - [x] Performance test to validate <2% p99 latency regression on small bursts Related: ENG-5234 (design), SUP-883 (support case exposing ambiguity in tool_choice), PM-112 (product acceptance criteria). This is intended to be non-breaking for existing customers: the framing defaults to an opt-in compatibility mode until a short feature flag rollout finishes and we run an automated migration to annotate live streams from the hosted fleet. See commits for implementation details.

review_comments: Daniel Rivera: Overall looks good; only concern is edge-case where two tools share identical schemas. Please add deterministic tie-breaker and an opt-out for legacy routing.
Marta Liu (author): Added deterministic tie-breaker (prefer warmer model/route) and feature-flag opt-out; updated tests to exercise tie scenarios.

Aisha Khan: Can we avoid adding more bytes to every stream fragment? Suggest compact binary header; otherwise good.
Marta Liu: switched header to concise ASCII envelope (14-40 bytes typical) to keep existing stream compatibility and ease SDK parsing.
Samir Patel: CI failed on first run due to flaky test test_framed_tool_stream; I saw you added a flake guard. Confirmed rerun passed and added a retry decorator for the e2e test.

notes_summary: Defines compact framed streaming envelope and deterministic routing fallback for OpenAI-style tool calls, adds schema mapper for robust validation, includes SDK parsing helpers and tests, feature-flagged rollout to avoid immediate breaking change.
